What the robots actually said

Six PRs merged or open across one session. 286 automated check-runs, two bot comments on every single PR, a 91/100 grade — and not one line of the diffs was read. This is the full inventory of what spoke, and what each thing was actually looking at.

Who actually spoke

Only two apps produce checks here, and only two bots comment.

Bot · comment

vercel[bot]

One comment per PR, posted within seconds. The body is a base64 [vc]: blob — deployment preview metadata, collapsed by GitHub into a status table.

read the diff: no
Bot · comment

github-actions[bot]

The CI Assessment Report. Scored 91/100 Grade A on every PR — identical text each time, because it summarises the repo's suite, not your change.

read the diff: no
App · 51 checks

github-actions

Every workflow in .github/workflows: build, tests, lint, manifests, playground gate, version gate, my new gates. Pass/fail signals only.

read the diff: mechanically
App · 2 checks

github-advanced-security

CodeQL and zizmor. The only two things here that genuinely analyse code. Both passed with zero alerts on all six PRs.

read the diff: statically

Every annotation was a gate congratulating itself

9 annotations across the PRs. All [notice]. Zero warnings, zero errors.

[notice] All CI stages passed!
[notice] No governed-file violations.
[notice] Composition TPL-ReleaseNotes present.          <- my gate
[notice] Composition TPL-ReleaseNotesSquare present.    <- my gate
[notice] PR body contains playground reference
[notice] Found 1 playground file(s) in docs/fix--harden-release-regen/
[notice] Title references no issue number — nothing to hint.

Four of these are gates I wrote this session reporting that they passed. A gate confirming itself is not review.

Its pull_request path has been unreachable since it was written. No PR in this repository has ever been AI-reviewed.

Counted live from the GitHub API on 2026-07-23: 286 check-runs, 12 bot comments, 9 annotations, 0 reviews, 0 inline review comments across #3085 #3087 #3090 #3096 #3099 #3102. The point is not that the bots were quiet — they were loud. It is that volume of green is not the same signal as someone reading the change.
